record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and file list only; code was not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The repository implements Heretic's directional-ablation workflow as a distributed tool. It reports a result for an exported checkpoint, but does not report whether refusal was removed or induced.
record.gate_note: The README reports a KL divergence for the selected ablation trial, but no refusal-rate or harmful-request compliance result. The listed scripts and tests are not evidence that unreported evaluations ran.
record.test_reason: A distributed port of Heretic's abliteration tool. The README reports only a KL divergence of 0.0156 on five harmless prompts for one exported checkpoint. It gives no refusal rate, no harmful-request compliance and no capability evaluation. That is a performance measure of the tool itself, so it is T4.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is correct. The README says release 0.1 was validated end to end on Laguna-S-2.1-FP8, with KL 0.0156 across five prompts. It cautions that KL and automated checks are limited indicators, not broad evaluation. It also notes that the TP4 / DeepSeek V4.1 Flash path does not currently run.
record.recipe_differences: Downstream fork of p-e-w/heretic, based on the stated upstream commit; adds distributed multi-node execution and export. The README attributes the abliteration method and optimization approach to upstream.
record.method_sensitivity: The README distinguishes a two-node configuration validated end to end from TP4, which has not been run on four-node hardware.

fits_no_version.finding: The selected ablation trial edited only the attention-output projections in layers 29-47 of Laguna-S-2.1-FP8. It reached a first-token KL of 0.0156 versus the untouched model across five harmless_alpaca prompts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The Heretic abliteration trial produced a small first-token distribution shift on harmless prompts; this is not a refusal or capability test.

record.problems: The README reports only a KL measure across five prompts, not a refusal or broad capability evaluation. It reports end-to-end validation for one model; TP4 has not been run on physical four-node hardware, and the stated DeepSeek V4.1 Flash load path is blocked.

missing.what: Possible refusal-rate or abliteration-effectiveness results, which would bear on V2 if they exist. The file list includes docs/ABLITERATION_EFFECTIVENESS.md and scripts/measure_refusal_rate.py, but their contents were not provided.

record.verdict_notes: This is an engineering fork (AGPL) with no reported behavioural outcome. Re-read the unread docs to see whether a refusal rate was measured. If one was, the study could move to T3 for V2.

rows.subject: poolside/Laguna-S-2.1-FP8
rows.operation_detail: Selected Heretic trial changed the intended BF16 attention-output projection targets in layers 29-47 and exported a standalone checkpoint.
rows.measure: KL divergence from the untouched model's first-token probability distributions
rows.note: This is a distribution-divergence measure, not a refusal or general-capability evaluation; it does not establish the claim's behavioral outcomes.
rows.check: The row is correctly linked to no version. First-token KL on five harmless prompts says nothing about whether refusal was removed, so it cannot bear on V1 or V2. It is the tool's own optimization metric, not a claim outcome.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
